subject: Auth & Key Management: Post-call action items and recommended options

Subject: Post-call recap: Auth & key-management options / next steps

Hi Tom / Sarah — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps based on our discussion (keeping it short):

- Call highlights: ClearBank is evaluating Redwood to handle embeddings + reranking for search, plus a small set of server-side generation endpoints for alerts. Primary constraints: regulator-driven auditability, 13+ month log retention, and integration with Okta for identity.

- Immediate asks we noted from your side:
  * Preferred auth model (you mentioned leaning to service accounts + short-lived tokens)
  * Rotation window: target <=30 days for any long-lived secrets, preference for automated rotation
  * Audit/logging retention and what evidence you need from us (token issuance logs, IPs, admin actions)
  * Network controls: IP allowlists, VPC peering options vs. private endpoints

Next steps (suggested):
1) Can you confirm which team/alias will own the security questionnaire follow-up? I’ll include them on the thread.
2) We’ll put together a concise options doc (API keys vs service accounts/OAuth/JWT) with tradeoffs, rotation recipes, and a recommended default for regulated workloads. Expect that in 24–36 hours. [attachment: redwood-auth-options.pdf]
3) If agreeable, run a 2-week sandbox POC: service account setup + embedding pipeline ingest (low QPS), exercise rotation and audit flows. We’ll provide config snippets for Okta/IdP and a sample service account policy.

For alignment: Marissa (solutions), Dev (platform) — help me draft the options doc (focus on rotation automation, KMS integration, and audit proofing). I’ve added the relevant items to the deal in HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DB-2026-0043

Tom/Sarah — any missing pieces or timeline constraints we should know about?

Thanks,
Jonas

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Auth & key-management options / next steps

Jonas — thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our platform/security POV:

- Identity provider: we use Okta (OIDC + SAML). Ideally we want service accounts issued by our IdP with short-lived JWTs that map to an internal service identity.
- Rotation: we cannot have any long-lived static secrets in production. Anything that looks like an API key must be short-lived or rotated by automation. Target is: automated rotation every 7–30 days depending on secret class.
- Audit requirements: token issuance events (who requested, which user/service), IPs, and revocation events need to be retained for 13 months. We’ll request signed statements or logs for SOC evidence during procurement.
- Embeddings / reranker: embeddings ingestion will come from a server-side job running in our analytics VPC — that job will make calls to Redwood endpoints. For that flow, we prefer using service accounts + JWTs rather than embedding server-side keys in CI. How do you handle both: (a) short-lived JWT auth for server agents, and (b) programmatic rotation for non-interactive CI tokens?
- Networking: we prefer private connectivity (VPC peering or PrivateLink). IP allowlisting is acceptable as a fallback.

Can you include a sample policy & config for the Okta -> Redwood service account exchange, and any constraints around key material storage? For us, customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) integration is required for any signing keys.

Attached our security contact listing and questionnaire extract: [attachment: clearbank-security-answers.docx]

—Tom

Jonas / Marissa — got it. Drafting recommended approach and tradeoffs below; attaching a sample service account policy and a short-play POC plan. [attachment: sample-service-account-policy.json]

Summary recommendation (short):
- For ClearBank (regulated, Okta, needs 13mo audit): recommend Service Accounts + short-lived JWTs, backed by customer-managed AWS KMS for signing where feasible. API keys are allowed only as a temporary fallback for non-critical dev environments.

Options & tradeoffs:
A) Service Accounts + JWT (recommended)
  * Pros: short-lived tokens, better auditability (we can tie token issuance to IdP assertion), simpler rotation model, recommended for production regulated workloads
  * Cons: requires IdP setup (Okta OIDC client), extra initial integration work; requires customer KMS if they need keys managed on their side

B) Rotating API keys (fallback)
  * Pros: simplest to implement; minimal IdP work
  * Cons: harder to meet "no long-lived secret" policy unless automated rotation is strictly enforced; weaker auditability unless combined with token issuance logs

Key implementation notes:
- Token lifetime: we recommend 15 minutes for JWTs used in high-frequency server calls, with a refresh flow that mints new tokens via an authenticated service account exchange.
- Rotation automation: Redwood exposes a rotation endpoint + webhooks. We can also support customer-side rotation orchestration (e.g., Lambda job) that calls Redwood RotateKey API on a schedule.
- Audit: we will surface token issuance events, IPs, and admin actions in Console. For procurement evidence, we can export signed token-issuance logs over the requested retention window.
- KMS: support for AWS KMS customer-managed keys for signing (we store only public key material if customer-managed signing is used; otherwise Redwood-managed keys are used with HSM protections).
- Networking: recommend PrivateLink / VPC peering for production. IP allowlist as interim step for POC.

Sample Okta flow (high level):
1) ClearBank creates an Okta OIDC app representing the Redwood service account client.
2) The server agent uses client credentials grant to obtain a short-lived token from Okta.
3) Redwood accepts the Okta-signed assertion (JWT) and issues a short-lived Redwood access token scoped to the service account.

Quick code snippets (pseudo):
# minting at client side (server agent)
POST https://clearbank.okta.com/oauth2/v1/token
  grant_type=client_credentials&scope=redwood:ingest
  Authorization: Basic <client-creds>

# Redwood exchange
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/exchange
  Authorization: Bearer <okta_jwt>
  body: {assertion: "<okta_jwt>", scope: "ingest"}

POC plan (2 weeks):
- Day 0–2: Exchange security questionnaire answers; get Okta test client + AWS test account access
- Day 3–6: Implement service account exchange and short-lived token path in sandbox; verify issuance logs
- Day 7–10: Run embedding ingestion job from ClearBank analytics VPC using service account flows; validate rotation and audit exports
- Day 11–14: Capture evidence artifacts (logs, sample signed export), review go/no-go

Deliverables: one-pager architecture diagram, sample Okta config snippets, sample-service-account-policy.json, rotation automation outline, and a two-week POC checklist. I’ve attached the policy draft and will update with concrete command examples once we have Okta metadata.

Let me know if you want me to package this into a short PDF for procurement. I can also join a technical sync with ClearBank security to walk the POC steps live.

Thanks —
